item.title: Quick Take — Veridical Data Science (audiobook)
item.description: This book is about practicing data science in a way that is genuinely trustworthy. The central argument is that getting useful, reliable results from data requires more than applying algorithms — it requires critical thinking, domain knowledge, and a principled framework for evaluating whether your results hold up. The authors call this veridical, meaning truthful, data science.
item.itunes:author: Bin Yu and Rebecca Barter

item.title: Ch. 1 — An Introduction to Veridical Data Science
item.description: To practice veridical data science is to practice "truthful" data science. The goal is to answer real-world questions by collecting and critically evaluating relevant empirical, data-driven evidence, using human judgment calls in the context of domain knowledge. If that evidence is deemed sufficiently trustworthy, it gets communicated to domain stakeholders, where it can play a role in real-world decision making and in updating what we know about the domain.
